title: TTF2 processes sites of incomplete DNA replication during mitosis via sister-chromatid exchanges.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. Checked: Europe PMC (closed access, no PMCID, no supplementary endpoint, no text-mined accessions); the NCBI 'pmc' link was a different, citing paper (PMC13657629, an eLife sister-chromatid-exchange method paper). Science landing page returns HTTP 403 (paywall). Searched PRIDE (ProteomeXchange proteomics archive) for 'Fujisawa', 'Labib', 'TTF2', 'TRAIP', 'MiDAS', 'mitotic replisome disassembly' and found no deposit for this study (the TRAIP hits are a Xenopus cross-linking deposit PXD058941 from a different paper, the Labib lab's USP37 deposit PXD056491, and the companion Walter-lab paper PXD055299). Searched GEO for TTF2+TRAIP and TTF2+sister chromatid exchange: 0 datasets. Downloaded and read the full matching bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.12.01.626218, Fujisawa & Labib, CC-BY, 474 kB HTML) including its methods and data-availability text, and listed its downloadable files: only the full PDF, no supplementary spreadsheets.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments: that the study is immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, immunoblots, microscopy, glycerol gradients, mass photometry and AlphaFold 3 predictions in mouse embryonic stem cells. The preprint states mass spectrometry data 'have been deposited at ProteomeXchange via PRIDE and will be made publicly available by the date of publication' but gives no accession, and I could not find one. Supplementary Tables S1-S3 are described in the preprint as showing 'selected factors' enriched in TRAIP immunoprecipitates, rendered as view-inline/PowerPoint image tables rather than machine-readable files; Table S4 is a reagent list.

a1_downloadable.note: Fails. No dataset is downloadable. The Science article and its supplement are paywalled (HTTP 403, not in PubMed Central), the promised PRIDE proteomics deposit has no locatable accession in PRIDE, ProteomeXchange search, GEO, or the paper metadata, and the open preprint offers only a PDF with image-style tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Fails. There is no prediction target anywhere: the outputs are blot intensities, microscopy images and hand-selected lists of co-purifying proteins. Any label (e.g. 'binds phosphorylated TRAIP') would have to be constructed by reading figures.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed in files - stopped at A1. The only machine-readable inputs implied are protein sequences of mouse TRAIP (UniProt Q8VIG6) and TTF2 (UniProt Q5NC05), i.e. two proteins, which would come from UniProt, not from this paper.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed - stopped at A1. The preprint reports arbitrary-unit blot quantification and masses in kDa; no measurement table with a units column exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fails on its face. This is a mechanistic cell-biology study: three independent immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry experiments plus blots and microscopy, far below the ~1,500 labelled rows needed. Exact row counts unknown because no table is accessible.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed - stopped at A1. Raw mass spectrometry files, if ever released, would be a few GB and are excluded by the project's no-raw-data rule.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable - no downloadable file exists to compare against the paper's numbers.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed - stopped at A1. Note that the structural content that looks most tabular (the TTF2 zinc-finger/phospho-TRAIP interface) is an AlphaFold 3 prediction, i.e. another model's output, which would be a circularity problem if used as a label.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would be the natural backbone for any phospho-binding task, but there is no data here to attach a head to

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. The paper carries two UniProt accessions (mouse TRAIP Q8VIG6, mouse TTF2 Q5NC05), which join to UniProt and AlphaFold DB, but two proteins is not a dataset.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper's data alone; the interesting question (which phospho-sites create binding surfaces for which reader domains) would need a phospho-interactome resource that this paper does not provide.

controls.external_validation: None - the companion Science paper (aeh1834, Walter/Pellman labs, proteomics deposit PXD055299) studies the same biology but is also mechanistic, not a labelled dataset.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper: its outputs are immunoblots, microscopy and three short lists of co-purifying proteins, so the only honest claim available is that the data does not support a predictive model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence around a phosphorylated site to predict whether a zinc-finger reader domain will bind it.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would need thousands of phospho-site/reader-domain pairs with measured binding; this paper supplies one such pair (phosphorylated TRAIP threonine 325 bound by the TTF2 zinc fingers), so the usable example count here is 1.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given phosphorylated residue is bound by a given reader domain, with the true answer coming from binding assays such as pull-downs or isothermal titration calorimetry. This paper's evidence is immunoblots of pull-downs, not a numeric table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying cell-cycle signalling would use a reliable phospho-reader predictor to decide which phosphorylation sites to mutate, but this paper cannot supply the training data for it.

ml_idea: No viable machine-learning project. The only idea the biology suggests - predicting which phosphorylated motifs are read by zinc-finger or other reader domains - would have to be built entirely from external resources (PhosphoSitePlus, PRIDE phospho-interactome studies, existing models such as DeepPhosPPI and PhosPPI-SEQ), with this paper contributing a single anecdotal example (phospho-TRAIP T325 bound by TTF2 zinc fingers).

effort.compute_note: Nothing estimated because no dataset exists to load; only the paywalled article and a CC-BY preprint PDF were available.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search PRIDE and GEO for a deposit from this paper and try the publisher's supplement - took about ten minutes and killed it: no accession, paywalled supplement, image-only tables.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic cell-biology paper with no downloadable dataset: Science supplement is paywalled, the promised PRIDE proteomics deposit has no findable accession, and the open preprint's tables are hand-picked protein lists rendered as images. Fails A1, and would fail A2 and A5 anyway since there is no label column and the experiment count is in the dozens, not thousands.
